ratings_why.fun: Every turn is a sequencing puzzle (who leads while you play, sell and end the turn), and Herald, Trailbreaker and The Front Lemming chain in ways the builds don't list; Tiers 1-3 feel flat, which holds it at 7.
ratings_why.distinct: Earns 8 over 7 because one rule, only your Front speaks, turns reading order into a queue of live texts in the fight and a turn-by-turn ordering puzzle while recruiting; no tribe today or generic auto-battler tribe plays like that.

verdict_why: The core is great, but Herding Council, Banner-Stitcher and Old Mother Lemen have rules a player can't resolve as written, and those are worth one pass.

points.text: Herding Council's text only works while it is a Front, but it is what makes the second Lemming a Front. If Council stands second, is it a Front? Say whether Council must be first, or that its text always applies.

Banner-Stitcher must be Front, yet playing a Lemming ahead of it takes the Front away. Say whether the trigger checks before or after the new unit lands. Either answer is a good puzzle; right now it can't be read.
Old Mother Lemen: do the Kits copy her Banner bonus, and what happens to Kit-Minder's buffs and to damage when she dies? The Matriarch build assumes answers the card doesn't give.

Herald copying an End of Turn text (Herding Elder, Banner-Bearer) or Herding Council is the tribe's best hidden combo. Pitch it in the builds so the owner sees it, and keep golden Herald copying two texts.

Tiers 1-3 are one job each, and only one of them speaks at a time. One early card that cares about its place in the queue (for example, gains stats when it takes the lead late) would give the early game a taste of the Relay.

standouts.why: Herald of the Herd lets two texts speak at once, and what it copies changes with every move, so it is a new card each turn.
Trailbreaker buffs and hands the lead on in one move, and chained Trailbreakers make a relay with a choice of order.
The Front Lemming doubles every later Take the Lead and then steps aside, so where you put it decides which leaders get doubled.

weakest.why: Tally is a gold piece that needs a mid-turn Front swap to sell Kits; it is fiddly for little and doesn't interact with anything else.
Kit-Minder competes for the End of Turn spot with Banner-Bearer and Herding Elder and mostly loses; its only twist is the Lemen anti-synergy.
Thaw Nester is a plain Kit maker whose only job is the early economy line.

flags.note: Cantor of the Edge doubled by The Front Lemming may stack two lasting effects, +4 per death, then golden Brother Onward gives twice that to everyone; check the Banner ceiling.
Gerd's "enemies attack your Front whenever they can": can they hit a Front in the back row while the front row lives?
Herding Council's text depends on Council being a Front, which its own text decides.
Banner-Stitcher's timing when the played Lemming becomes the new Front is not stated.
Whether Old Mother Lemen's Kits copy her Banner bonus is not stated.
